root_cause: The offcanvas component conditionally activates the focus trap only when the scroll option is false. With data-bs-scroll="true" (as used in the help panel), the focus trap is not activated, allowing focus to leave the modal when tabbing.
repair_strategy: Modify the show method in offcanvas.js to always activate the focus trap, removing the conditional check on the scroll configuration.
expected_accessibility_effect: When the help panel is opened, pressing Tab will keep focus inside the panel, cycling among its focusable elements (the close button and any other controls) instead of moving to the underlying page.
functional_risks: Potential minor change in tab order for users who previously could tab to background elements while the offcanvas was open with scroll enabled; this aligns with modal dialog expectations and is not a functional regression.
verification_requirements: After opening the help panel, the first Tab press moves focus to the close button (#help-close).
Subsequent Tab presses cycle focus within the panel and do not shift focus to elements outside the panel (e.g., the amount input).
Closing the panel via the close button or Escape restores focus to the trigger button.
Screen readers announce the panel as a dialog and trap navigation inside it.
